Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Subobject.Lattice gives SemilatticeInf,
SemilatticeSup, and OrderTop on Subobject Y under standard limit
hypotheses. I can't find a HeytingAlgebra instance for the case
where Y is an object of an elementary topos (HasClassifier C).

  1. Does this instance exist somewhere I'm missing, or is there a PR
    in flight?

  2. If it's genuinely absent, any reason it hasn't been added? The
    Mac Lane–Moerdijk IV.8 construction (pseudo-complement via the
    classifier) looks like a few hundred lines of routine topos
    theory.

it's not there, and afaik there is no PR working on this (directly). I'm currently in the process of getting mathlib ready (in the sense that i have PRs with preliminaries) for my code proving the fundamental theorem of topos theory, which i believe will add some useful machinery for proving this fact.
the PRs are going slowly on my part because i have to juggle my studies too, in case anyone is wondering why they're awaiting-author

Thanks, that confirms what I was seeing.

A few questions if you have a moment:

  1. Could you point at the PRs in flight? Useful to follow them,
    and I might be able to help with reviews.

  2. Do you think the Heyting instance for Subobject Y is best
    contributed as a downstream PR once your preliminaries land, or
    could it land in parallel? I don't want to step on the
    infrastructure you're building.

  3. Any gaps your preliminaries are filling that would also feed
    into the Heyting construction? (E.g., classifier-based pullback
    machinery, internal logic infrastructure.)

Asking because a separate project assumes this instance locally;
if it became derivable from HasClassifier it would clean up
several files. Not blocking, just trying to understand the right
order of operations.

• #37045: partial map diagrams
  • #37844: bicategory of partial maps
  • #38130: pullbacks in cartesian monoidal categories
as for 2, i don't know. i haven't read maclane-moerdijk :face_with_peeking_eye:, i'm merely following Jaap van Oosten's lecture notes for topos theory

there's a bunch of side interests that i formalized along the way, you can check it out in my scratch project, notably the Ops folder (about internal logical operators) seems relevant to this topic in particular

Thanks I went through Classifier/Semilattice.lean and the Ops/ folder. The SemilatticeInf and the Imp Heyting adjunction on (X ⟶ Ω) are very close to what we need (we land on Subobject Y in an elementary topos for a partition theorem in a separate project, but the order-isomorphism transport is standard). For now we're keeping our Heyting-gated lemmas sorry-stated against the gap rather than building a parallel Subobject version locally, and tracking CwFTT as the closest existing scaffold. If you end up working on Or.lean or the HeytingAlgebra wrap-up and want a hand with Or or the Subobject bridge, happy to coordinate. Otherwise no expectation, and good luck with the partial-map and pullback PRs.
I realised that we do have docs#CategoryTheory.Subobject.instCompleteLattice, so in theory you could try to extend that?
Although then the problem will be proving that elementary topoi satisfy those conditions, probably

Thanks. So the path is instCompleteLattice → Order.Frame → HeytingAlgebra via the existing instance graph, and the real work becomes proving the frame law on Subobject Y in an elementary topos. That follows from pullback preserving colimits standard topos theory but apparently not yet threaded through the Subobject API.

Three technical paths now look viable: Mac Lane–Moerdijk IV.8 direct pseudo-complement construction, your instCompleteLattice → Frame extension, and your CwFTT (X ⟶ Ω) work transported via the classifier order-iso. I've logged this in our project's upstream-dependency note.

Many thanks
Out of curiosity and to avoid potential duplicated efforts, could I ask what are you working on @Chris Brink ?

Thanks for asking. Short version: I'm formalizing a four-cell partition theorem on Subobject (D.obj Y) in an elementary topos. The four cells are defined by Heyting predicates over a fixed "kernel image" subobject Im(η) — namely ≤ Im(η) (Infrastructure), straddling Im(η) and its complement (Distribution), ≤ Im(η)ᶜᶜ ∧ ¬(≤ Im(η)) (Exploitation, the closure-residue), and ≤ Im(η)ᶜ (Refusal). The theorem and per-cell disjointness corollaries are the Lean payload. The framework that uses the partition (FalseWork) maps it onto structural readings of canonical works across cinema, music, physics, software, etc., but the Lean piece is self-contained and doesn't depend on the framework.

The gating issue is what Edward and I have been discussing: HeytingAlgebra (Subobject Y) for elementary topoi isn't in Mathlib yet. Six of my proofs reduce to standard Heyting identities (aᶜ ⊓ aᶜᶜ = ⊥ and similar) and stop short without that instance. Three technical paths look viable — Mac Lane–Moerdijk IV.8 direct construction, extending instCompleteLattice to Order.Frame (Edward's afternoon suggestion), or transporting from his CwFTT (X ⟶ Ω) work via the classifier order-iso. I'm in sorry-state-and-cite for now while a parallel project takes priority, so no duplication risk from my side — I'm not actively building the upstream instance, just consuming whatever lands.

What are you working on? And since you're at Utrecht under Paige North I'd be curious whether there's any departmental interest in the HeytingAlgebra (Subobject Y) gap from a different angle (type-theoretic, HoTT, presheaf, whatever).

Lean lives at https://github.com/thefalsework/papers/tree/main/lean — HEYTING-GAP.md has the upstream dependency and the three paths in more detail than I'm putting here.
PR open: #39618. Construction is per Mac Lane–Moerdijk IV.6 Proposition 2 as we discussed. Thanks again for the gap-confirmation discussion.
